title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression from Scratch: the nbzinbCirkovic Package
text: Count outcomes, number physician visits number published articles, often modelled Poisson regression. Poisson model forces variance equal mean. Real count data usually violate two ways: variance much larger mean (overdispersion), zeros Poisson distribution mean produce (excess zeros). Ignoring overdispersion makes standard errors small tests anti-conservative. negative binomial (NB) model adds dispersion parameter θ\theta lets variance exceed mean. zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model goes treats data mixture group always produces zeros group follows NB distribution. goal project R package, nbzinbCirkovic, fits models without general-purpose optimizer. NB regression fitted iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) alternated Newton–Raphson log⁡θ\log\theta, ZINB regression EM algorithm whose M-steps IRLS fits. show package reproduces MASS::glm.nb() pscl::zeroinfl(), check simulation zinbreg() recovers known parameters, use analyze physician office visits NMES1988 data.

title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression from Scratch: the nbzinbCirkovic Package
text: package exports two fitting functions control functions: nbreg(formula, data, offset, control = nbreg_control()) zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control = zinbreg_control()), two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2 (count covariates |, zero-model covariates ; without | parts use covariates). Internally, R/irls.R holds IRLS Newton–Raphson building blocks, nb_fit() NB outer loop (reused, weights 1−τi1-\tau_i, ZINB count M-step), zinb_fit() EM loop, R/hessian.R analytic derivatives. functions return S3 objects ("nbreg", "zinbreg") methods print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik (df attribute, AIC() BIC() work), fitted, residuals (response Pearson), nobs predict (newdata; zinbreg, type = "response", "count" "zero"). control functions set tolerances, iteration limits trace option; fitting functions warn algorithm converge θ̂\hat\theta large (Poisson limit). package roxygen2 documentation runnable examples, four testthat files compare glm.nb() zeroinfl() check offsets, single-covariate models, error messages monotone EM log-likelihood, GitHub Actions workflow running R CMD check Linux, macOS Windows. Installation short example:
code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("cirkovicdavid/nbzinbCirkovic") library(nbzinbCirkovic) fit <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment, data = bioChemists) summary(fit) predict(fit, newdata = bioChemists[1:3, ], type = "zero")
